title: Anchor Runway & Micro-KPI experiment notes
content:
Context:
Quick scratchpad for a 6-week personal experiment to extend productive "runway" (days/weeks I can sustain focused output) and test a set of micro-KPIs that feel predictive of progress. Not a polished OKR doc — fast notes, questions, and actions.

Why this experiment:
- Last quarter I burned out in week 7 of a deep project; energy dropped even though objectives were clear. Want to productize my personal pacing: shorter cycles, better early warning signals, and a small set of metrics to course-correct.
- Hypothesis: Tracking 3 micro-KPIs (focus-hours, decision latency, and weekly momentum items) will let me detect a declining runway 7-10 days earlier than my intuition. That will let me reduce load (or swap tasks) and avoid burnout.

Baseline (week of 2026-02-09):
- Focus-hours (deep work blocks >=45m): 14h/week (target 18)
- Decision latency (avg time from idea -> decision or triage): ~3.4 days
- Momentum items (meaningful progress events: merged PRs, shipped demos, customer follow-ups): 5/week
- Sleep: 6.3h/night (variability +1.2h)
- Energy index (self 1-10): avg 6.2

Targets for 6-week run:
- Focus-hours: increase to 18h/wk by week 3, sustain 16h+ thereafter
- Decision latency: reduce to <=48h on triageable items
- Momentum items: 7/week baseline, with an emphasis on quality (1 demo or synthesis per week)
- Sleep: average >=7h/night

Signals and thresholds (auto-alert rules for myself):
- If focus-hours week-over-week drops >20% -> mandatory 1-day buffer and replan
- If decision latency >72h for 3+ items -> block 2 hours for triage
- If energy index <=5 for two consecutive days -> swap to low-cognitive tasks and sleep priority

Experiment plan (week-by-week):
- Week 0 (prep): set trackers, add 45m deep-blocks to calendar, communicate to close collaborators (Liam/Sofia) that I'm running this experiment.
- Weeks 1-2: ramp focus blocks, practice 2x weekly 15m decisions-only reviews (clear inbox of decisions), log daily energy and quick note about friction.
- Weeks 3-4: evaluate prefix cache: reuse micro-prompts and templates to reduce friction (template PR descriptions, meeting agendas). Run a 1hr retrospective at end of week 4.
- Weeks 5-6: test a small policy change: one 2-day deep-window (no meetings) vs normal week and compare metrics.

Daily quick template (copy into 10s journal):
- Top 3 priorities (1 line)
- Deep blocks scheduled (count)
- Energy (1-10) + sleep hours
- One friction note (what slowed me)

Measurement approach:
- Manual daily log in a single lightweight note (this doc or a daily file).
- Weekly rollup on Sunday: numbers + short 6-sentence retrospective.
- Slack ping to collaborators at mid-run (week 3) with a 2-line status update.

Reflections / hypotheses to test:
- H1: Decision latency is the earliest proxy for overload — I expect it to spike before focus-hours fall. If true, scheduling regular decision triage will extend runway.
- H2: Templates (PR/meeting) will reduce decision latency by ~30% and reduce mental overhead; measurable via median triage time.
- H3: A single 2-day deep-window will result in a net +10% momentum items across the week even if focus-hours look similar (consolidation benefit).

Risks and constraints:
- External meeting load from cross-team ops can break the schedule; mitigation: preemptively block 2x 60m meeting-free slots per week and mark them immutable.
- Overemphasis on countable wins (PRs) may bias toward small, low-value work. Add weekly qualitative check: "did this move product/customer/learning forward?"

Quick action list (first 7 days):
- [ ] Add recurring 45m deep-blocks Mon/Wed/Fri + 2 flexible blocks Tues/Thurs
- [ ] Create a tiny spreadsheet or note with fields: date, focus-hours, energy, decisions-latency, momentum-items
- [ ] Draft 3 standard PR templates and one 5-min meeting agenda template
- [ ] Tell Liam + Sofia via Slack that I'm experimenting and ask for 1 mid-run check-in

Open questions / notes to self:
- How to count "momentum items" precisely? For now: PR merged, demo recorded, customer reply that moves opportunity forward, or design decision documented. Could refine later.
- Should I weight items by impact? Maybe keep simple for the first run.
- If energy stays low but focus-hours stay high, this suggests compensating behavior (pushing through). Consider a mandatory rest-day trigger.

Mini retrospective (after week 1, 2026-02-17):
- Focus-hours: 15h (up 1h)
- Decision latency: 2.6 days (improved)
- Momentum: 6 items
- Notes: Templates helped, but meetings ate two intended deep blocks. Need to claim one immovable slot. Energy avg 6.0.

Next steps (short):
- Tweak calendar invites to make one block non-negotiable (label: "Focus Runway")
- Push PR template to GH draft repo and reuse it twice this week
- Re-evaluate sleep hygiene (reduce evening screen time)

Longer-term thought: create a tiny dashboard (manual table or simple script) to visualize these 3 metrics week-over-week and surface the first sign of runway erosion on a single card. If this run shows promising leading indicators, formalize into a 3-week cadence template for future projects.

Notes-to-self end: keep it playful, this is a data-informed guardrail, not a performance police. Track kindness metric too: did I protect time to recharge? (yes/no)
